guide.summary: A big, slow grazer that sweeps algae and yeast out of the water.
guide.biology: Rotifers are tiny many-celled animals with a crown of beating hairs that pulls a current of water, and the food in it, into their mouths.
guide.rules: Lives in water. Moves 0.7 cells per second and notices prey up to 3 cells away. Its filter feeding is simplified: it catches one prey on contact, stores it as a meal of up to twice its own body, and waits 4 seconds before the next catch. Stops hunting when well fed. Eats Sunbead, Glasswheel, Shadeleaf, Turnleaf, Bubble and Creambud; never eats bacteria. Nothing in the dish eats it.
guide.example: Add a few Rotifers to a green Sunbead dish and watch whether the algae thin out, then whether the Rotifers run short of food.
